 424B4
 Anthropic, PBC - 424(b)(4) 
 Filed Pursuant to Rule 424(b)(4) 
 Registration Nos. 333-299633 and 333-300148 
 Class A Common Stock | 980,000,000 Shares | Anthropic, PBC
 This is an initial public offering of shares of Class A common stock of Anthropic, PBC. We are selling 956,351,354 shares of Class A common stock and the selling 
 stockholders identified in this prospectus are selling an additional 23,648,646 shares of Class A common stock. We will not receive any proceeds from the sale of shares 
 of our Class A common stock by any of the selling stockholders. 
 Prior to this offering, there has been no public market for our Class A common stock. The initial public offering price per share is $83.00 . We have been approved to list 
 our Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol “ANT.” 
 We have a novel capital and corporate governance structure. We are incorporated as a public benefit corporation under Delaware law, a structure consistent with our 
 commitment to artificial intelligence (“AI”) safety and responsibility. As a public benefit corporation, we are required to balance the pecuniary interests of our 
 stockholders, the best interests of those materially affected by our conduct, and the specific public benefit purpose identified in our amended and restated certificate of 
 incorporation: the responsible development and maintenance of advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity. We created our Long-Term Benefit Trust (the 
 “LTBT”) to help ensure that Anthropic, PBC is managed in a manner that responsibly balances its goals as a public benefit corporation. The LTBT is intended to operate 
 as an independent body of financially disinterested trustees with expertise in AI safety, national security, public policy, and social enterprise. Through a special class of 
 common stock, Class T common stock, the LTBT generally has the authority to elect and remove the Class T directors, who together will constitute a majority of the 
 authorized members of our board of directors. Our Class T common stock does not otherwise have voting rights with respect to matters submitted to stockholders 
 generally and has no economic rights. Immediately prior to the completion of this offering, we will also issue a single share of Class F common stock, a special class of 
 our common stock, to a limited liability company organized by our co-founders (the “Founder LLC”). Dario Amodei, our Chief Executive Officer and a member of our 
 board of directors, and Daniela Amodei, our President and Chairperson of our board of directors, together with our five other co-founders, will initially be the sole 
 members of the Founder LLC. Our Class F common stock, which will be held by the Founder LLC, will be entitled to an aggregate number of votes that equals 50.1% of 
 the total voting power of our outstanding shares of capital stock with respect to matters submitted to stockholders generally, including the election of our directors other 
 than the Class T directors. Our Class F common stock will not have any economic rights. Immediately prior to the completion of this offering, we will also authorize a 
 special class of our common stock, Class E common stock, which will be issued to our employees, excluding our co-founders. Our Class E common stock will be entitled 
 to vote only on certain limited matters and will not have any economic rights. In addition, we have authorized Class A common stock and Class N common stock. The 
 rights of the holders of Class A common stock and Class N common stock are identical, except with respect to voting and conversion. Each share of Class A common 
 stock is entitled to one vote and shares of Class N common stock have no voting rights, except as otherwise required by law. The holders of our Class N common stock are 
 primarily strategic business partners, and shares of Class N common stock will generally convert to Class A common stock upon a sale or transfer to an unaffiliated third 
 party. Our Class A common stock is not convertible. See the sections titled “Risk Factors—Risks Related to our Governance Structure,” “Our Governance Structure and 
 Its Goals,” and “Description of Capital Stock” for more information. 
 We are considered a “controlled company” within the meaning of the Nasdaq Global Select Market corporate governance requirements. See the sections titled “Our 
 Governance Structure and Its Goals,” “Management,” and “Description of Capital Stock” for additional information. 
 See the section titled “ Risk Factors ” beginning on page 30 to read about factors you should consider before buying shares of our Class A 
 common stock. 
 Neither the Securities and Exchange Commission nor any other regulatory body has approved or disapproved of these securities or 
 passed upon the accuracy or adequacy of this prospectus. Any representation to the contrary is a criminal offense.

 (1) The underwriters will not receive any discount or commission on any shares of our Class A common stock sold pursuant to their option to purchase additional shares of Class A 
 common stock from us. See the section titled “Underwriting” for a description of the compensation payable to the underwriters . 
 To the extent that the underwriters sell more than 980,000,000 shares of Class A common stock, the underwriters have the option to purchase up to an 
 additional 147,000,000 shares of Class A common stock from Anthropic, PBC at the initial public offering price. 
 The underwriters expect to deliver the shares against payment in New York, New York, on or about November 20, 2026.
